newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sovereign eyeing financing for manganese.
newsitem.headline: Sovereign eyeing financing for manganese.

text.p: Sovereign Resources (Australia) NL said on Wednesday it was examining financing options for the development of a manganese sulphate project based on its Ant Hill mine project in Western Australia.
Sovereign said it had appointed Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's BHP Engineering Pty Ltd to conduct a full bankable feasibility study on the project.
As part of study BHP is to carry out a full engineering and marketing study on the Ant Hill project, the company said.

A scoping study has already concluded that the project could generate A$12 million in revenue a year, yielding an operating surplus of A$6.4 million a year over a 20-year plus mine life, Sovereign said.
The project has a forecast capital cost of A$7.5 million.
The manganese sulphate plant would be constructed at Port Hedland, in Western Australia's Pilbara region, with ore transported by truck 340 km from the Ant Hill propspect, Sovereign said.
The Ant Hill deposit hosts a resource of 1.4 million tonnes of ore, grading an average of 25 percent manganese, the company said.
Manganese sulphate is mainly used as a stock feed and fertiliser, as well as a primary feedstock for the production of downstream products such as manganese dioxide used in dry cell batteries.
Sovereign said it expected the feasibility study to be completed before the end of December this year.
